findings.headline: 99215 on 27.6% of 1,655 claims vs 2.2% expected; 7 of 8 sampled 99215 charts documented below billed level
findings.interpretation: Risk-adjusted score 31.0, the highest in the book. 72% of 99215s are on patients with 0-1 chronic conditions. In the random sample of 29 usable charts, 11 (38%) were documented below the billed level, against a 3% peer rate. Draft overpayment estimate from the random sample: $22,447 (CI $16,254-$28,640). Needs certified coder re-review.

findings.headline: 99215 on 22.8% vs 1.9% expected; 91% of 99215s on patients with 0-1 conditions; notes look inflated, with audit-trail signs
findings.interpretation: The charts mostly support the billed level (1 of 30 below). But 57% of notes address fewer problems than the billed level implies, 37% are duplicates, and the audit trail we received shows 17% bulk-created and 27% paste-heavy notes. 5 of 22 notes claiming moderate-or-higher data review have no test line on the claim. This fits notes written up to match the bill, not sicker patients. Because the charts support the billed level, the draft overpayment estimate is small ($449, CI $0-$1,188). The draft summary says no audit trail was received; that is wrong, one was received in round 2. Recovery should wait for a coder re-score.

findings.headline: 99215 on 25.9% vs 3.2% expected; charts support billing but notes show inflation signs
findings.interpretation: 1 of 30 charts was below the billed level. Signs of possible inflation: notes claim data review that the claims do not back (20-23%), problems shortfall 43%, duplicates 30%, audit trail 17% bulk-created and 23% paste-heavy. 99215 share is high in every complexity stratum. This is a priority for coder review of the cited notes; the evidence does not yet support an upcoding finding.
